$comment: Trusted Types sinks in the admin bundle and why each is acceptable. Checked by packages/csp/bin/bundle-sinks.mjs; see docs/trusted-types-plan.md.

sinks.DOMParser.parseFromString npm:dompurify: DOMPurify's own parse, given TrustedHTML from its own 'dompurify' policy, which the header allows.
sinks.DOMParser.parseFromString packages/csp/s: The default policy's comparison parse, given TrustedHTML from hangar-inert.
sinks.dangerouslySetInnerHTML npm:next-themes: The anti-flash script. The copy that runs is the one served in the document, allowed by hash or nonce; React's client re-render does not execute and the default policy recognises it (KNOWN_LIBRARY_SCRIPTS).
sinks.dangerouslySetInnerHTML npm:react-dom: React's implementation of the prop; its callers are the other dangerouslySetInnerHTML entries here.
sinks.dangerouslySetInnerHTML npm:react-router: <Scripts>' inline context and module loader: served in the document and allowed by hash (web, admin) or nonce (space); client re-renders go through the default policy.
sinks.eval npm:lodash: Function('return this') global detection, never reached in a browser (globalThis exists); refused anyway by script-src, which has no 'unsafe-eval'.
sinks.eval npm:lodash-es: Function('return this') global detection, never reached in a browser (globalThis exists); refused anyway by script-src, which has no 'unsafe-eval'.
sinks.innerHTML npm:@bprogress/core: The progress bar's constant template; goes through the default policy, which DOMPurify leaves unchanged.
sinks.innerHTML npm:dompurify: DOMPurify's own parse, given TrustedHTML from its own 'dompurify' policy.
sinks.innerHTML npm:react-dom: dangerouslySetInnerHTML and React's inert creation of script elements; plain strings go through the default policy.
sinks.script element npm:react-dom: React creates script elements for rendered and hoisted scripts; client-rendered ones do not execute, and script text or URLs go through the default policy.
